cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Balance – a state where different things are equal.

p.em: Example: A good balance between work and sleep is important.

cosy-blockquote.p: Career – a job that you do for a long time.

p.em: Example: She wants a long career as a school teacher.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overtime – extra hours that you work at your job.

p.em: Example: He works overtime to get more money.

cosy-blockquote.p: Relaxation – time to rest and feel calm.

p.em: Example: Reading a book is my favorite relaxation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stress – a feeling of worry or pressure.

p.em: Example: Too much work can cause a lot of stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Busy – having a lot of work or things to do.

p.em: Example: I am very busy with work today.

cosy-blockquote.p: Holiday – a time when you do not work and can travel.

p.em: Example: They are going to Spain for their summer holiday.

cosy-blockquote.p: Free time – time when you do not have to work or study.

p.em: Example: In my free time, I like to play football.

cosy-blockquote.p: Office – a room or building where people work at desks.

p.em: Example: My office is very near the train station.

cosy-blockquote.p: Task – a small job that you must do.

p.em: Example: Cleaning the kitchen is my daily task.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why must we maintain a healthy work-life balance to protect our mental health?
★ What is the most important thing for your daily balance?

Why should a person think twice before committing to a demanding career?
★ Do you want to change your career in the future?

How much overtime must employees work in your country's corporate culture?
★ Did you work overtime last week?

Why should deep breathing be your primary method of relaxation?
★ How do you relax after a very busy day?

When work causes too much stress, what immediate steps should you take?
★ What causes you the most stress at work or school?

How busy must your schedule be before you decide you have to take a break?
★ Are you busy this weekend, or do you have free time?

Why should families spend their holiday entirely disconnected from work emails?
★ Where did you go for your last holiday?

What urgent tasks have to be completed before you can enjoy your free time?
★ What free-time activities do you do with your family?

Why must a modern office design quiet relaxation spaces for its employees?
★ Is your current office comfortable for you?

Which difficult task should you delegate to others to reduce your stress?
★ What is your most difficult task today?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: ⏳ Activity 1: The Work-Life Scale How do you balance your day? Together with your partner, evaluate these three daily duties. Discuss how much time we should give to each. Practice using modals of obligation (must, have to, should): 💼 Office Job & Tasks We have to complete our tasks, but we should not work overtime every day. 😴 Sleep & Health To avoid stress, an adult must sleep 7 to 8 hours every night. 🧘 Relaxation & Hobbies You should spend some free time in nature to completely recharge. 🚫 Closing: The Digital Detach Promise As we celebrate National Workaholics Day, we promise to set boundaries. Which promise would help you reduce stress the most? 📵 No work emails after 7:00 PM 🏖️ Taking a full 10-day offline holiday 🚲 No laptop or screens on Sundays 💤 Dedicating 1 hour daily to a creative hobby

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, we must have a good balance between work and rest.
★ How do you keep a good balance when your smartphone is always in your pocket?

In the future, we will not have to be too busy with jobs to have money.
★ If you never had to be busy with jobs, what would you do to feel useful?

When robots do every difficult task, humans should learn to rest more.
★ Have you ever felt anxious during a day without any task to do?

We will not need a physical office, so we must learn to work from home.
★ Do you work better when there is a clear boundary between your office and your bedroom?

Bosses must help workers reduce stress and take more breaks.
★ Would you feel comfortable if your boss could track your emotional stress in real-time?

We should stop working too much overtime because it is bad for us.
★ Have you ever worked overtime to avoid dealing with personal life problems?

We should look at how people enjoy their free time, not just their jobs.
★ What creative activity would you pursue if you had unlimited free time?

Older people must stop working sooner so they can enjoy a long holiday.
★ At what age do you hope to stop working and start your permanent holiday?

A good career should also allow you to have a family.
★ Do you think it is easy to have a good job and a happy family?

We have to get more time for relaxation when machines do our work.
★ If you could redesign the workweek for better relaxation, how many hours would be ideal?

ul.li: Incorrect: I have a busy job → Correct: I have a demanding job ((Demanding is better for jobs than busy))
Incorrect: I am work in office → Correct: I work in an office ((Simple present tense structure))
Incorrect: He work very hard → Correct: He works very hard ((Third-person singular 's'))
